content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/jack/src/agent-workflows/plugins/agent-workflows/skills/do-task

# Do the task

Target: 501 — the claimed issue, or the one just picked up.

**This writes; it does not judge.** It ends with a commit or a captured act, and a plain
statement of what state the work is in. Deciding whether that state is *done* belongs to
the pass after this one — an author grading their own work grades it done, which is why the
grading is somebody else's.

**Two modes, and the issue already says which.** Work ending in a diff writes files and
commits them. Work ending in evidence performs an act and records that it happened. A
certificate rotation produces no patch; the record of the commands and their output is the
only proof it occurred.

## 0. Which platform

Derive it — `git remote get-url origin`. Only the verbs this skill needs:

| | GitHub — `gh` | GitLab — `glab` |
|---|---|---|
| comment | `gh issue comment <N> --body "…"` | `glab issue note <N> -m "…"` |
| close with evidence | `gh issue close <N> --comment "…"` | **two commands** — `glab issue note <N> -m "…"` then `glab issue close <N>` |

**`glab issue close` takes no comment.** Note first, close second. Reversed, a failed note
leaves a closed issue with no record of what was done — and a closed issue is the one nobody
looks at again.

## 1. Know what you are doing

Read the claim before touching anything: the issue, its comments, the reading `take-issue`
stated, and the branch — or the absence of one, which means this ends in evidence.

**No claim to read?** "Just fix it" is what people actually type, and it arrives with no
assignee, no stated reading, and often no issue. That is workable, not an error — say which
you have and carry on:

| What is missing | What to do |
|---|---|
| the branch | Decide the mode yourself: does this end in a diff or in evidence? |
| the stated reading | Read the issue and state your own before starting. It is the cheap moment |
| the issue itself | Do the work if it is small. If it is not, say so — untracked work of any size is invisible the moment this session ends |

Never invent a claim. Reporting an issue as claimed when nothing on the platform says so is
worse than working without one.

**Three sources, three authorities.** They disagree more often than anyone expects:

| Source | Binds on |
|---|---|
| the code | **reality** — what is true now, whatever anything says |
| the issue | **scope** — what this change may touch |
| the log | **nothing.** It informs |

A log that seems to forbid something is not a constraint; it is a previous person's
situation, recorded under conditions that may no longer hold. Where the issue and the code
disagree about what exists, the code is right and the issue needs a comment.

## 2. Hold the scope

**`Out of scope` is binding.** It is the one section written specifically to stop the next
person widening the work, and that next person is now you.

Finding something else worth doing is normal and is not permission. File it, or say it in
the report, and carry on with what was claimed. A change that quietly grew is a change
nobody agreed to, and it is the review that pays for it.

Where the issue's scope turns out to be wrong rather than merely narrow — the fix is
impossible inside it — stop and say so. That is a finding, not an obstacle to route around.

## 3. Do it

**Ending in a diff:** write the change. Run whatever the project runs — tests, typecheck,
build — and run it because a claim is verified when it was observed, not when it was
expected.

**Ending in evidence:** work the procedure the issue gives, in order. Where a step is
destructive or order-dependent, do not vary it. Capture as you go rather than
reconstructing afterwards:

- the commands, exactly as run
- their output, verbatim
- the state before and after
- when, and by whom

**Verify from outside the change.** Checking with the tool that made it proves the tool
ran, not that the world changed. A different vantage point is the whole value of the check.

**Stop on a surprise.** A precondition that is false, an output that does not match, a step
that fails halfway — these end the run and go into the report. An operation abandoned
mid-procedure leaves the system in neither state, and the report is what tells someone.

## 4. Record it

**A diff:** commit to the claimed branch, citing the issue.

The message carries **why**, not only what — the diff already shows what. Code says what it
does and tests say what it is for, but nothing except this message says why it was done this
way rather than the other way. When the code is deleted, its story goes with it and the
message is what survives.

**Evidence:** put it on the issue, then close it — note first, close second, per step 0. The
issue is the only place this act is recorded, so the comment carries the commands, the
output and the before-and-after state, not a summary of them.

**Do not close an issue that ends in a diff.** The change request closes it on merge, and
closing by hand strands the branch.

## 5. Say what state it is in

Not a verdict — a state, honestly named. The pass after this one routes on it, and it can
only route on the truth:

| State | What it means |
|---|---|
| **done** | The acceptance line is satisfied, and you checked rather than assumed |
| **half done** | Real progress, the rest is clear and doable |
| **stuck** | Blocked on something you cannot resolve — say what, and who can |
| **more than one task** | This is two or more pieces of work wearing one issue number |
| **not started** | A precondition failed before anything was touched |

**"Done" is the claim that costs most to get wrong**, because everything downstream trusts
it. Everything else is cheap to say and cheap to act on.

## Noticing other issues

While in here you will see issues that are already satisfied, stale, or done by something
else. **Say so; never close them.** An issue that looks done can be a false positive, and
closing one wrongly removes it from the board while the work stands undone.

One line in the report: *"#38 looks already satisfied by <evidence>; close it?"* That is a
board tidied by work already happening, rather than a sweep nobody reaches for.

## Steps

Copy this checklist and tick each item as you finish it:

    Task Progress:
    - [ ] Platform derived from the git remote, not assumed
    - [ ] Claim read — issue, comments, the stated reading, branch or no branch
    - [ ] Mode known: ends in a diff, or ends in evidence
    - [ ] Work done, and verified from outside itself
    - [ ] Recorded — committed with why, or evidence on the issue then closed
    - [ ] Scope held; anything found outside it reported, not absorbed
    - [ ] State named honestly, not graded
    - [ ] Other issues noticed along the way — offered, never closed

## Report

Two lines and a question:

    HALF DONE — parser fixed and tested; the error message rewrite is untouched.
    Next: finish the message rewrite, ~20 min.
    Run it, or see what changed?

An evidence run reports the same way, with what proves it:

    DONE — cert rotated on staging, expiry now 2027-02-14, verified from an external probe.
    Next: nothing. #51 closed with the commands and output attached.

A surprise is a state, and reads the same:

    STUCK — the migration needs a maintenance window nobody has scheduled.
    Next: someone books the window, then this resumes from step 3.

The two states easiest to leave unsaid, because neither feels like a result:

    MORE THAN ONE TASK — #47 is a schema change and a UI change; they ship separately.
    Next: split it, then take the schema half.

    NOT STARTED — the staging database is already on 16, so the precondition is false.
    Next: someone confirms whether #52 is stale before anything runs.

The diff, the commands, the output and the trace are prepared and held until asked.

## Why this scenario exists

The build/runtime/inference suites prove the *stack* works; this scenario proves each supported
**model** actually runs on K80 (compute 3.7) — coherent output, real GPU memory, the expected
GPU count, and no `CUBLAS_STATUS` / `CUDA error`, with the model unloaded afterwards to free VRAM
for the next. It is the per-model regression half of [STORY-005](../stories/STORY-005.md). Each
case is one model; `Script:` carries the real `TC-MODELS-*.yml` (the YAML ids have gaps where
cases were retired and run to `024`).

Models are chosen **one tag per code path** — engine (Ollama vs llama.cpp) × architecture ×
GGUF layout (vision inline or a split projector) × any size-gated branch — using the smallest tag
that reaches the path. A new model gets a case only when it reaches a path no case covers yet.

Every case runs the same four steps unless noted, at `temperature` 0 with a fixed
`seed` so the answer is reproducible:

| # | Action | Expected Result |
|---|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Test inference | `response` contains a 4; no `CUBLAS_STATUS` / `CUDA error` |
| 2 | Check GPU memory | reports non-zero `MiB` in use |
| 3 | Check GPU count | `GPU_COUNT_OK` (not `GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED`) |
| 4 | Unload model | `Model unloaded` |

content.content:
id: TC-MODELS-016
name: gemma4:12b Multimodal Inference
suite: models
priority: 4
timeout: 1200000
dependencies: []
issue: 367
intent:
  user_story: |
    Verify gemma4:12b answers text, image and audio prompts on the K80

steps:
  - name: Warm up (tolerate transient cold-load retry under suite GPU pressure)
    command: |
      # ~10GB split across 2 K80 dies; under back-to-back-model GPU pressure the first cold load
      # can crash ("llama runner terminated") and ollama auto-retries. Absorb that here so the
      # real assertions below run against the loaded model.
      for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
        r=$(curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \
          -d '{"model":"gemma4:12b","prompt":"hi","stream":false,"options":{"num_predict":1}}')
        echo "$r" | grep -q '"response"' && { echo "WARM_OK"; break; }
        echo "warm attempt $i: $(echo "$r" | head -c 120)"; sleep 8
      done
    expectPatterns:
      - "WARM_OK"
    rejectPatterns:
      - "CUBLAS_STATUS"
      - "CUDA error"

  - name: Text inference
    command: |
      out=$(curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \
        -d '{"model":"gemma4:12b","prompt":"What is 2+2? Reply with only the number, no punctuation.","stream":false,"options":{"num_predict":400,"temperature":0,"seed":0}}')
      echo "$out" | head -c 2000
      echo "$out" | jq -e '.error == null and .response == "4"' >/dev/null \
        && echo "ANSWER_OK" || echo "ANSWER_FAIL"
    expectPatterns:
      - "ANSWER_OK"
    rejectPatterns:
      - "ANSWER_FAIL"
      - "CUBLAS_STATUS"
      - "CUDA error"

  - name: GPU offload check (must be on GPU, not CPU)
    command: docker exec ollama37 nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
    expectPatterns:
      - "[0-9]+ MiB"

  - name: Vision inference
    command: |
      IMG=$(python3 - <<'PY'
      import base64, struct, zlib
      # 224x224 RGB: white disc on black (a simple, describable shape)
      w=h=224; px=bytearray()
      for y in range(h):
          px.append(0)  # PNG filter byte per row
          for x in range(w):
              d=((x-112)**2+(y-112)**2)**0.5
              v=255 if d<70 else 0
              px += bytes((v,v,v))
      def chunk(t,d):
          c=t+d; return struct.pack('>I',len(d))+c+struct.pack('>I',zlib.crc32(c)&0xffffffff)
      png=b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'+chunk(b'IHDR',struct.pack('>IIBBBBB',w,h,8,2,0,0,0))+chunk(b'IDAT',zlib.compress(bytes(px)))+chunk(b'IEND',b'')
      print(base64.b64encode(png).decode())
      PY
      )

id: TC-MODELS-016
name: gemma4:12b Multimodal Inference
suite: models
priority: 4
timeout: 1200000
dependencies: []
issue: 367
intent:
  user_story: |
    Verify gemma4:12b answers text, image and audio prompts on the K80

steps:
  - name: Warm up (tolerate transient cold-load retry under suite GPU pressure)
    command: |
      # ~10GB split across 2 K80 dies; under back-to-back-model GPU pressure the first cold load
      # can crash ("llama runner terminated") and ollama auto-retries. Absorb that here so the
      # real assertions below run against the loaded model.
      for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
        r=$(curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \
          -d '{"model":"gemma4:12b","prompt":"hi","stream":false,"options":{"num_predict":1}}')
        echo "$r" | grep -q '"response"' && { echo "WARM_OK"; break; }
        echo "warm attempt $i: $(echo "$r" | head -c 120)"; sleep 8
      done
    expectPatterns:
      - "WARM_OK"
    rejectPatterns:
      - "CUBLAS_STATUS"
      - "CUDA error"

  - name: Text inference
    command: |
      out=$(curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \
        -d '{"model":"gemma4:12b","prompt":"What is 2+2? Answer in one short sentence.","stream":false,"options":{"num_predict":400,"temperature":0,"seed":0}}')
      echo "$out" | jq -r '"response: " + (.response // "" | .[0:400])'
      echo "$out" | jq -c '{error, done, done_reason, eval_count}'
      { [ -n "$out" ] && echo "$out" | jq -e '.error == null and .done == true' >/dev/null 2>&1; } \
        && echo "LOAD_OK" || echo "LOAD_FAIL"
    expectPatterns:
      - "LOAD_OK"
    rejectPatterns:
      - "LOAD_FAIL"
      - "CUBLAS_STATUS"
      - "CUDA error"

  - name: GPU offload check (must be on GPU, not CPU)
    command: docker exec ollama37 nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
    expectPatterns:
      - "[0-9]+ MiB"

  - name: Vision inference
    command: |
      IMG=$(python3 - <<'PY'
      import base64, struct, zlib
      # 224x224 RGB: white disc on black (a simple, describable shape)
      w=h=224; px=bytearray()
      for y in range(h):
          px.append(0)  # PNG filter byte per row
          for x in range(w):
              d=((x-112)**2+(y-112)**2)**0.5
              v=255 if d<70 else 0
              px += bytes((v,v,v))
      def chunk(t,d):
          c=t+d; return struct.pack('>I',len(d))+c+struct.pack('>I',zlib.crc32(c)&0xffffffff)
      png=b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'+chunk(b'IHDR',struct.pack('>IIBBBBB',w,h,8,2,0,0,0))+chunk(b'IDAT',zlib.compress(bytes(px)))+chunk(b'IEND',b'')
      print(base64.b64encode(png).decode())
      PY
      )
      out=$(curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/chat \
        -d "{\"model\":\"gemma4:12b\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"What shape is in this image? Reply with one lowercase word, no punctuation.\",\"images\":[\"$IMG\"]}],\"stream\":false,\"options\":{\"num_predict\":400}}")
      echo "$out" | jq -r '"content: " + (.message.content // "" | .[0:400])'
      echo "$out" | jq -c '{error, done, done_reason, eval_count}'
      { [ -n "$out" ] && echo "$out" | jq -e '.error == null and .done == true' >/dev/null 2>&1; } \
        && echo "VISION_OK" || echo "VISION_FAIL"
    expectPatterns:
      # the request reached the vision path and came back; whether the shape is
      # named is the agent judge's call, and it reads "content" above
      - "VISION_OK"
    rejectPatterns:
      - "VISION_FAIL"
      - "CUBLAS_STATUS"
      - "CUDA error"
      - "does not support"
      - "cannot see|can't see|unable to see|no image"

  - name: Audio inference (spoken word)
    command: |
      command -v espeak-ng >/dev/null || { echo "espeak-ng missing on this host"; echo "AUDIO_FAIL"; exit 1; }
      espeak-ng -s 130 -w /tmp/tc016_audio.wav "hello hello hello" 2>/dev/null
      python3 -c "import base64,json; b=base64.b64encode(open('/tmp/tc016_audio.wav','rb').read()).decode(); json.dump({'model':'gemma4:12b','messages':[{'role':'user','content':'Which word is spoken in this audio? Reply with one lowercase word, no punctuation.','images':[b]}],'stream':False,'options':{'num_predict':400}}, open('/tmp/tc016_req.json','w'))"
      out=$(curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/chat -d @/tmp/tc016_req.json)
      echo "$out" | jq -r '"content: " + (.message.content // "" | .[0:400])'
      echo "$out" | jq -c '{error, done, done_reason, eval_count}'
      { [ -n "$out" ] && echo "$out" | jq -e '.error == null and .done == true' >/dev/null 2>&1; } \
        && echo "AUDIO_OK" || echo "AUDIO_FAIL"
    expectPatterns:
      # the request reached the audio path and came back; transcription accuracy is
      # marginal on synthetic speech and was never a load gate
      - "AUDIO_OK"
    rejectPatterns:
      - "AUDIO_FAIL"
      - "CUBLAS_STATUS"
      - "CUDA error"
      - "does not support audio"
      - "cannot hear|can't hear|text-based|text-only|no audio|don't have the ability"

  - name: Unload model
    command: |
      curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \
        -d '{"model":"gemma4:12b","keep_alive":0}'
      echo "Model unloaded"
    expectPatterns:
      - "Model unloaded"

name: Models Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      test_id:
        description: "Run a single test by ID (e.g. TC-MODELS-013)"
        required: false
        type: string
      judge_mode:
        description: "Test judge mode (dual = SimpleJudge + agent judge, the default; simple = load and crash checks only)"
        required: false
        default: "dual"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "dual"
      debug:
        description: "Enable OLLAMA_DEBUG=1 in container"
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean
      runner_label:
        description: "Which GPU testbed to run on. sm37 = Tesla K80 (reference). sm75 = RTX 2060 (most models exceed its VRAM)."
        required: false
        default: "sm37"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "sm37"
          - "sm75"
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      judge_mode:
        description: "Test judge mode (dual = SimpleJudge + agent judge, the default; simple)"
        required: false
        default: "dual"
        type: string
      debug:
        description: "Enable OLLAMA_DEBUG=1 in container"
        required: false
        default: false
        type: boolean
      runner_label:
        description: "Which GPU testbed to run on"
        required: false
        default: "sm37"
        type: string
    outputs:
      result:
        description: "Models test result"
        value: ${{ jobs.models.outputs.result }}

jobs:
  models:
    name: Models Tests
    runs-on: [self-hosted, "${{ inputs.runner_label || 'sm37' }}"]
    environment: cicd-1
    env:
      OLLAMA37_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}
      OLLAMA_DEBUG: ${{ inputs.debug && '1' || '' }}
    outputs:
      result: ${{ steps.models-tests.outcome }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Identify host
        uses: ./.github/actions/identify-host

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Install test runner dependencies
        run: cd cicd/tests && npm ci

      - name: Run models tests
        id: models-tests
        env:
          # dual mode runs the keyless agent judge; the runner reads JUDGE_MODE.
          JUDGE_MODE: ${{ inputs.judge_mode || 'dual' }}
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          # JUDGE_BASE_URL (cicd-1 variable) points the judge at an ollama server
          # instead of Anthropic — a judge off the box under test. Unset it and
          # the judge falls back to Claude on the OAuth token above; the auth
          # token has to follow the base URL or it would break that fallback.
          ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL }}
          ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && 'ollama' || '' }}
          ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && vars.JUDGE_MODEL || '' }}
          # Claude Code's side-call model; ollama has no haiku tag to serve it.
          ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && vars.JUDGE_MODEL || '' }}
        run: |
          cd cicd/tests
          echo "Judge mode: ${JUDGE_MODE}"

          # Build test ID flag if provided
          ID_FLAG=""
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.test_id }}" ]; then
            ID_FLAG="--id ${{ inputs.test_id }}"
            echo "Running single test: ${{ inputs.test_id }}"
          fi

          # Run models tests
          rc=0
          bash ../scripts/gpu-temp-guard.sh -- npx tsx src/cli.ts run --suite models $ID_FLAG --format json > /tmp/models-results.json || rc=$?
          [ "$rc" -eq 75 ] && exit 1   # overheat → fail the job; any other non-zero stays tolerated (gated by the JSON below)

          echo "--- JSON Results ---"
          cat /tmp/models-results.json

      - name: Check test results
        run: |
          FAILED=$(jq '.summary.failed' /tmp/models-results.json)
          echo "Failed tests: $FAILED"
          if [ "$FAILED" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::$FAILED models test(s) failed"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Unload test models from VRAM
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "Unloading test models from VRAM..."
          # Derived from the suite, so adding or removing a testcase needs no edit here.
          for m in $(grep -ohE '"model":"[^"]+"' cicd/tests/testcases/models/*.yml | cut -d'"' -f4 | sort -u); do
            curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"keep_alive\":0}" || true
          done
          echo "Models unloaded"

      - name: Upload models results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: models-test-results
          path: |
            /tmp/models-results.json
            cicd/results/

### TC-16: lfm2.5:8b (Liquid LFM2 MoE)

- **Objective:** lfm2.5:8b — the text LFM2 **MoE** (8B total / ~1B active, ~5.2 GB) — runs on K80 compute 3.7 (single GPU). **The two judges assert different things.** The simple judge asks whether the model loaded
and the request survived — an `{"error":…}` body, a missing `done`, an empty body or a CUDA
error is a failure, and the reply's text is not its business. The agent judge reads the reply
and asks whether it is language a person could read; **a wrong answer is a pass**, because a
270M model getting arithmetic wrong says nothing about the K80. That is why the suite defaults
to `judge_mode: dual` — under `simple` alone nothing checks the output at all.

The prompt asks for a sentence rather than a bare number, so there is language to judge.

Every case runs the same four steps unless noted, at `temperature` 0 with a fixed
`seed` so the run is reproducible:

| # | Action | Expected Result |
|---|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Test inference | `LOAD_OK` — no `{"error":…}`, `done` true, no `CUBLAS_STATUS` / `CUDA error`. The agent judge reads the `response` |
| 2 | Check GPU memory | reports non-zero `MiB` in use |
| 3 | Check GPU count | `GPU_COUNT_OK` (not `GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED`) |
| 4 | Unload model | `Model unloaded` |

- **Objective:** gemma4:12b — the only gemma4 packaged as a **split-vision** model (a separate `projector` blob, vs the embedded projector in e4b/26b) — loads on the **new engine** and runs on K80 compute 3.7. Step 1 is the acceptance gate.
- **Script:** cicd/tests/testcases/models/TC-MODELS-016.yml

Six steps, not four — it is the only case that exercises image and audio input:

| # | Action | Expected Result |
|---|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Warm up | `WARM_OK` — absorbs the cold-load retry under suite GPU pressure |
| 2 | Text inference | `LOAD_OK` — no `{"error":…}`, `done` true; no `unknown model architecture: 'gemma4'` fallback, no `CUBLAS_STATUS` / `CUDA error` |
| 3 | GPU offload check | reports non-zero `MiB` in use |
| 4 | Vision inference | `VISION_OK` — the request reached the vision path and returned; no refusal (`cannot see`, `does not support`). The agent judge reads the `content` and asks whether it describes something seen |
| 5 | Audio inference | `AUDIO_OK` — `espeak-ng` present, the request returned, no refusal. Transcription accuracy is not gated: synthetic speech is marginal |
| 6 | Unload model | `Model unloaded` |

test(models): split the judges — simple for load, agent for language

A models case asserted the answer's text, so gemma3:270m answering "2"
to 2+2 was a CI regression while every step exited 0, the weights were
resident and the model unloaded cleanly. Nothing about the K80 was
broken; a 270M model got a sum wrong. The exact match could not pass
that model at all — it ends replies with "\n", so even "4" arrived as
"4\n".

Each judge now asserts what it is good at. The simple judge asks
whether the model loaded and the request survived: no {"error":...},
done true, a non-empty body, no CUDA error. It reads nothing of the
reply's text. The agent judge reads the reply and asks whether it is
language a person could read — a wrong answer passes, an empty or
repetitive one does not.

That moves the output check onto a judge that was opt-in, so the suite
now defaults to judge_mode: dual. Under simple alone nothing would
check the output at all. The cost is a dependency on the judge server
being up, which is the tradeoff this records.

Two supporting changes the split needs:

The prompt asks for a sentence instead of a bare number. A single
digit gives the agent judge nothing to call language.

The step prints the reply field first and the envelope second, rather
than 2000 characters of raw body. The judge truncates each step's
stdout at 1000 characters, and a thinking model's reasoning span
pushed the answer past that — the judge was being asked about a reply
it could not see.

TC-MODELS-016's vision and audio steps stop asserting "circle" and
"hello" for the same reason, and its espeak-ng dependency is now
checked rather than silently passing on an error body (#498 case 3).

Verified on the K80: TC-MODELS-008 passes with gemma3:270m; a
fabricated empty reply fails the agent judge while the simple judge
passes it; a model that cannot load fails the simple judge alone.

Refs #501

Three things I want to flag now rather than bury:

- **I changed the prompt**, as you chose: `"What is 2+2? Answer in one short sentence."` That makes #501's criterion 1 no longer demonstrable in its literal wording — with the sentence prompt, gemma3:270m answers *correctly* ("2 + 2 = 4"). The behaviour the criterion protects is intact and proven by the empty-reply probe, but the issue text should be corrected rather than quietly left wrong.

The agent judge truncates each step's stdout at 1000 characters, so for thinking models the reasoning span pushed the answer out of view — the judge was being asked about a reply it could not see. This touches #498's territory without changing the harness.
- **#498's third case is stale.** It says the audio step passes because `espeak-ng` is absent from the runner. `espeak-ng` is installed now (`/usr/bin/espeak-ng`), so that argument no longer holds. I've made the step check for it explicitly instead of failing obscurely. I did not touch #498 — that's yours to close or amend.

content.text:
**HALF DONE — five of six criteria met and committed; the suite run was killed at case 9 of 19 by the GPU temperature guard, and my change is the likely cause.**
**Next:** decide how to get a full green run — rerun cold, run in halves, or shorten what the models generate.

| Criterion | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Wrong answer passes | Met | TC-MODELS-008 passes locally |
| 2. Empty reply fails the agent judge | Met | Fabricated empty reply: simple PASS, agent FAIL naming the empty output |
| 3. Load failure fails the simple judge alone | Met | `no-such-model:99b`, agent judge off, simple FAIL |
| 4. Models suite defaults to dual | Met | Dispatch and `workflow_call` both; `simple` still selectable |
| 5. Suite green on the K80 | **Not met** | Run [35549667518](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/actions/runs/35549667518) aborted: `peak 81°C exceeded 80°C` |
| 6. Spec doc matches | Met | Step-1 expectation, the judge split, and TC-15's six-step table |

**The thermal abort is probably mine, and I'd rather say so than call it flaky.** The last full green run peaked at 75°C; this one hit 81°C and was killed. No earlier models run in the visible history tripped the guard. The likely mechanism is the prompt change you picked: asking for a sentence instead of a bare number means every model generates far more tokens — a thinking model like deepseek-r1 went from a handful to 343 — so the suite does substantially more GPU work back to back. The nine cases that did run all passed every step; no case failed on its assertions.

The guard did its job, so I don't propose weakening it. The per-host knob (`GPU_TEMP_LIMIT`) belongs where that host's jobs are defined, and changing it to make my own change pass would be exactly the loosening criterion 5 warns against.

Three ways forward, and this is your call:

1. **Rerun now that the cards are cooling** (61/55/46/46°C). Cheapest test of whether 81°C was a one-off caused by back-to-back runs today rather than by the change itself.
2. **Cap the generation.** Drop `num_predict` from 400 to something like 80 for the non-thinking cases. One sentence needs far less than 400 tokens; the budget was set when the answer was a single digit.
3. **Split the suite** into two dispatches so the cards get a break between halves.

Branch `issue-501-judge-split` is pushed at `5fe2a275`. Nothing is merged, and #501 stays open.

#!/bin/bash
# gpu-temp-guard.sh - run a command under a K80 GPU temperature guard.
#
# Runs <command>, polling nvidia-smi for the hottest GPU die. If it crosses the
# threshold, the command (and its whole process group) is killed and the script
# exits 75 - a distinct "overheat" code the caller can act on. Otherwise it exits
# with the command's own code. Either way the peak temperature is appended to
# $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY (and stderr), so every run records how hot it got.
#
# Usage: gpu-temp-guard.sh [--threshold N] [--interval S] -- <command> [args...]
#
# Knobs (flags override env):
#   --threshold / GPU_TEMP_LIMIT     hard abort, °C   (default 80)
#   --interval  / GPU_TEMP_INTERVAL  poll period, s   (default 10)
set -u

OVERHEAT_RC=75
MAX_UNREADABLE=3        # consecutive unreadable polls -> abort (a hung driver / GPU off the bus is
                        # exactly what an overheat causes; blindly continuing defeats the guard)
threshold="${GPU_TEMP_LIMIT:-80}"
interval="${GPU_TEMP_INTERVAL:-10}"

usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 [--threshold N] [--interval S] -- <command> [args...]" >&2
}

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in
        --threshold) [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "gpu-temp-guard: --threshold needs a value" >&2; usage; exit 2; }; threshold="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --interval)  [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "gpu-temp-guard: --interval needs a value"  >&2; usage; exit 2; }; interval="$2";  shift 2 ;;

jobs:
  models:
    name: Models Tests
    runs-on: [self-hosted, "${{ inputs.runner_label || 'sm37' }}"]
    environment: cicd-1
    env:
      OLLAMA37_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}
      OLLAMA_DEBUG: ${{ inputs.debug && '1' || '' }}
    outputs:
      result: ${{ steps.models-tests.outcome }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Identify host
        uses: ./.github/actions/identify-host

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Install test runner dependencies
        run: cd cicd/tests && npm ci

      - name: Run models tests
        id: models-tests
        env:
          # dual mode runs the keyless agent judge; the runner reads JUDGE_MODE.
          JUDGE_MODE: ${{ inputs.judge_mode || 'dual' }}
          CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          # JUDGE_BASE_URL (cicd-1 variable) points the judge at an ollama server
          # instead of Anthropic — a judge off the box under test. Unset it and
          # the judge falls back to Claude on the OAuth token above; the auth
          # token has to follow the base URL or it would break that fallback.
          ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL }}
          ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && 'ollama' || '' }}
          ANTHROPIC_MODEL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && vars.JUDGE_MODEL || '' }}
          # Claude Code's side-call model; ollama has no haiku tag to serve it.
          ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: ${{ vars.JUDGE_BASE_URL && vars.JUDGE_MODEL || '' }}
        run: |
          cd cicd/tests
          echo "Judge mode: ${JUDGE_MODE}"

          # Build test ID flag if provided
          ID_FLAG=""
          if [ -n "${{ inputs.test_id }}" ]; then
            ID_FLAG="--id ${{ inputs.test_id }}"
            echo "Running single test: ${{ inputs.test_id }}"
          fi

          # Run models tests
          rc=0
          bash ../scripts/gpu-temp-guard.sh -- npx tsx src/cli.ts run --suite models $ID_FLAG --format json > /tmp/models-results.json || rc=$?
          [ "$rc" -eq 75 ] && exit 1   # overheat → fail the job; any other non-zero stays tolerated (gated by the JSON below)

          echo "--- JSON Results ---"
          cat /tmp/models-results.json

      - name: Check test results
        run: |
          FAILED=$(jq '.summary.failed' /tmp/models-results.json)
          echo "Failed tests: $FAILED"
          if [ "$FAILED" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::$FAILED models test(s) failed"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Unload test models from VRAM
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "Unloading test models from VRAM..."
          # Derived from the suite, so adding or removing a testcase needs no edit here.
          for m in $(grep -ohE '"model":"[^"]+"' cicd/tests/testcases/models/*.yml | cut -d'"' -f4 | sort -u); do
            curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate -d "{\"model\":\"$m\",\"keep_alive\":0}" || true
          done
          echo "Models unloaded"

      - name: Upload models results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: models-test-results
          path: |
            /tmp/models-results.json
            cicd/results/

test(models): pin the sampler on TC-MODELS-016's vision and audio requests

Every request in the suite runs at temperature 0 with seed 0 so a run
reproduces — except these two, which were missed. Under the old
assertions that did not show: a pattern matched the thinking span, so
any reply passed.

With the agent judge reading the reply, it shows. Run 35551629359 had
the vision step spend all 400 tokens without answering (content empty,
done_reason "length"), and the agent judge failed it. Rerunning the
same request by hand without a sampler gave "arc", then
"heart<channel|>heart"; with temperature 0 and seed 0 it gave "circle"
in 6 tokens, twice.

This removes the nondeterminism, not the check: an empty or refused
reply still fails.

Refs #501
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <[REDACTED-email]>
EOF

input.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re
OLD = '''      output=$(docker exec ollama37 nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv,noheader)
      echo "$output"
      active=$(echo "$output" | grep -c 'MiB')
      total=$(echo "$output" | grep -oP '[0-9]+(?= MiB)' | paste -sd+ | bc)
      echo "Active GPUs: $active, Total VRAM: ${total} MiB"
      if [ "$active" -le 1 ]; then
        echo "GPU_COUNT_OK"
      elif [ "$total" -le $(( (active - 1) * 11441 )) ]; then
        echo "GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED: total ${total} MiB fits in $((active - 1)) GPUs but using $active"
      else
        echo "GPU_COUNT_OK"
      fi
'''
NEW = '''      # Die placement is not deterministic across loads: now and then a model spills a
      # small allocation onto one die more than it needs. Reload once before calling
      # it a regression; overshooting twice is one.
      die_check() {
        output=$(docker exec ollama37 nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv,noheader)
        echo "$output"
        active=$(echo "$output" | grep -c 'MiB')
        total=$(echo "$output" | grep -oP '[0-9]+(?= MiB)' | paste -sd+ | bc)
        echo "Active GPUs: $active, Total VRAM: ${total} MiB"
        [ "$active" -le 1 ] || [ "$total" -gt $(( (active - 1) * 11441 )) ]
      }
      if die_check; then
        echo "GPU_COUNT_OK"
      else
        echo "RELOAD: ${total} MiB fits in $((active - 1)) GPUs but using $active; reloading once"
        curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate -d '{"model":"%(model)s","keep_alive":0}' >/dev/null
        curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \\
          -d '%(payload)s' >/dev/null
        if die_check; then
          echo "GPU_COUNT_OK (after one reload)"
        else
          echo "GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED: total ${total} MiB fits in $((active - 1)) GPUs but using $active, twice"
        fi
      fi
'''
done = []
for p in sorted(pathlib.Path('cicd/tests/testcases/models').glob('*.yml')):
    t = p.read_text()
    if OLD not in t:
        continue
    payload = re.search(r"-d '(\{\"model\":\"[^\"]+\",\"prompt\":[^']+)'\)", t).group(1)
    model = re.search(r'"model":"([^"]+)"', payload).group(1)
    p.write_text(t.replace(OLD, NEW % {'model': model, 'payload': payload}))
    done.append(f"{p.name}:{model}")
print(len(done)); print("\n".join(done))
PY

content.content:
- name: Check GPU count
    command: |
      output=$(docker exec ollama37 nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv,noheader)
      echo "$output"
      active=$(echo "$output" | grep -c 'MiB')
      total=$(echo "$output" | grep -oP '[0-9]+(?= MiB)' | paste -sd+ | bc)
      echo "Active GPUs: $active, Total VRAM: ${total} MiB"
      # ornith:35b (~22.8 GB) is ~99.5% of two K80 dies — too tight for real KV/context growth,
      # so a 3-die split is expected and correct ("can't safely fit two -> use three"). Only flag
      # waste if the model would fit in (active-1) dies with ~10% headroom to spare.
      if [ "$active" -le 1 ]; then
        echo "GPU_COUNT_OK"
      elif [ "$total" -le $(( (active - 1) * 11441 * 9 / 10 )) ]; then
        echo "GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED: total ${total} MiB fits in $((active - 1)) GPUs (with headroom) but using $active"
      else
        echo "GPU_COUNT_OK"
      fi
    expectPatterns:
      - "GPU_COUNT_OK"
    rejectPatterns:

# ornith:35b (~22.8 GB) is ~99.5% of two K80 dies — too tight for real KV/context growth,
      # so a 3-die split is expected and correct ("can't safely fit two -> use three"). Only flag
      # waste if the model would fit in (active-1) dies with ~10% headroom to spare.
      # Die placement is not deterministic across loads: now and then a model spills a

        echo "GPU_COUNT_OK"

        echo "RELOAD: ${total} MiB fits in $((active - 1)) GPUs (with headroom) but using $active; reloading once"

        if die_check; then
          echo "GPU_COUNT_OK (after one reload)"
        else
          echo "GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED: total ${total} MiB fits in $((active - 1)) GPUs (with headroom) but using $active, twice"
        fi
      fi

id: TC-MODELS-019
name: "ornith:35b Inference"
suite: models
priority: 3
timeout: 900000
dependencies: []
issue: ""
intent:
  user_story: |
    Verify ornith:35b answers on the K80

steps:
  - name: Test inference
    command: |
      out=$(curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/generate \
        -d '{"model":"ornith:35b","prompt":"What is 2+2? Answer in one short sentence.","stream":false,"options":{"num_predict":400,"temperature":0,"seed":0}}')
      echo "$out" | jq -r '"response: " + (.response // "" | .[0:400])'
      echo "$out" | jq -c '{error, done, done_reason, eval_count}'
      { [ -n "$out" ] && echo "$out" | jq -e '.error == null and .done == true' >/dev/null 2>&1; } \
        && echo "LOAD_OK" || echo "LOAD_FAIL"
    expectPatterns:
      - "LOAD_OK"
    rejectPatterns:
      - "LOAD_FAIL"
      - "CUBLAS_STATUS"
      - "CUDA error"

  - name: Check GPU memory
    command: docker exec ollama37 nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
    expectPatterns:
      - "[0-9]+ MiB"

  - name: Check GPU count
    command: |

        echo "GPU_COUNT_OK"
      fi

    rejectPatterns:

19	Models are chosen **one tag per code path** — engine (Ollama vs llama.cpp) × architecture ×
20	GGUF layout (vision inline or a split projector) × any size-gated branch — using the smallest tag
21	that reaches the path. A new model gets a case only when it reaches a path no case covers yet.
22	
23	**The two judges assert different things.** The simple judge asks whether the model loaded
24	and the request survived — an `{"error":…}` body, a missing `done`, an empty body or a CUDA
25	error is a failure, and the reply's text is not its business. The agent judge reads the reply
26	and asks whether it is language a person could read; **a wrong answer is a pass**, because a
27	270M model getting arithmetic wrong says nothing about the K80. That is why the suite defaults
28	to `judge_mode: dual` — under `simple` alone nothing checks the output at all.
29	
30	The prompt asks for a sentence rather than a bare number, so there is language to judge.

import yaml,glob

test(models): give the die-count check one reload before it fails

Run 35551629359 failed TC-MODELS-001 on GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED: gpt-oss:20b
put a 93 MiB allocation on a third die. The same load on the same
image lands on two dies locally and on rerun. Placement is not
deterministic, and it is not specific to one model — any case with a
die check can flake the whole suite this way.

On an overshoot the check now unloads the model, repeats the step-1

Four answers, in your order.

**1. Parser leak — nothing to do.** The script already overcomes it: with the sampler pinned, gemma4:12b answers "circle" and the `<channel|>` leak never appears. No library work. I saved your rule — script first, library only when no script answer exists — as a memory for future sessions.

**2. Die-count retry — done, committed `5a835086`.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Behaviour** | On an overshoot: unload, repeat the step-1 request byte for byte, check again. A second overshoot still fails |
| **Visible, not silent** | Prints `RELOAD: …` and passes as `GPU_COUNT_OK (after one reload)`, so the log and the agent judge both see a retry happened |
| **Coverage** | All 18 cases with a die check. TC-019 keeps its own 90% headroom threshold for ornith's expected 3-die split |
| **Verified** | All four branches with stubbed GPU output (clean, one flake, two flakes, single die), plus TC-001 on the real K80. Each reload request is checked identical to its step 1 |
| **Found on the way** | TS-04 had never documented TC-019 or TC-021. Added, so the spec covers all 19 cases |

**3. `workflow-patterns.md` — yes, keep it, and a rewrite is the right call.**
- **Only copy of the trigger rule.** It's the only place that says why no workflow runs on `push` or `pull_request`: self-hosted runners on a public repo would let a fork run code on your K80. I grepped every other doc and skill and found it nowhere else.
- **Loaded exactly when needed.** It's path-scoped to `.github/workflows/**`, so an agent reads it at the moment it's about to add such a trigger.
- **The rest is mixed:**
  - Unique and worth keeping: host selection by label, `identify-host`, per-host knobs.
  - Duplicated: the suite and perf catalog is repeated in `cicd/README.md` and the `ollama37-ci-perf` skill.
  - Stale: judge mode now defaults to dual, `JUDGE_BASE_URL` routing is missing, and it still says the models suite uses the temperature guard.

  I'd suggest the rewrite keep the unique rules, fix the stale parts, and drop the catalog.

**4. Agent judge quality — right verdicts, weak justification.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Accuracy** | 21 verdicts across this work, none wrong that I can find. Both real failures were caught with specific reasons: TC-016's empty vision reply, TC-001's third die. The empty-reply probe too. I read all 21 replies it passed; each is sensible |
| **Passes don't show the work** | All 17 passes read "All criteria met", with no quote of the reply. On a pass you can't tell whether it read the reply or pattern-matched the step results |
| **Cost** | About 44 s per verdict — 14 min of judging on top of a 33 min suite |
| **Quirk** | Every reply sends the JSON twice (19 of 19). Harmless, wasted tokens |
| **Not independent on load** | For TC-001 it failed on `GPU_COUNT_EXCEEDED`, the simple judge's own finding. Fine by the criteria, but there it adds no second opinion |

The fix I'd suggest: make `evidence` required on pass too — "quote the reply you judged". That's one line in `agent-judge.ts`'s response spec, and it makes every pass auditable. It touches all suites, not just models, so I haven't done it.

**Branch state:** `issue-501-judge-split`, 5 commits, pushed. There has still been no single all-green full-suite run, and the retry hasn't been through a full CI run yet. That's the natural next step before a PR.

Base directory for this skill: /home/jack/src/agent-workflows/plugins/agent-workflows/skills/open-pr

# Open the change request

Target:  — the issue this change closes, if there is one.

**This makes work reviewable. It does not decide whether the work is good.** That judgment
happened already; re-litigating it here means two passes disagreeing with nobody to settle
it. What this checks is mechanical: is the work committed, is it on a branch that is not the
default, does the body link the issue correctly.

**Evidence work never arrives here.** An act performed leaves no diff to review, and its
issue was closed where the act happened. If there is no branch, this is the wrong unit.

## 0. Which platform

Derive it from `git remote get-url origin`.

| | GitHub — `gh` | GitLab — `glab` |
|---|---|---|
| create | `gh pr create --title "…" --body "…"` | `glab mr create --title "…" --description "…"` |
| target branch | `-B/--base` | `--target-branch` |
| draft | `-d/--draft` | `--draft` |
| body template | `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` | `.gitlab/merge_request_templates/`, via `--template` |
| read it back | `gh pr view <N> --json body,url` | `glab mr view <N>` |

**`-d` means different things.** It is `--draft` on `gh` and `--description` on `glab`.
A command copied between them changes meaning without erroring, which is the worst kind of
difference. Write the long flags.

## 1. Is there anything to push

Four checks, and each has a distinct answer when it fails:

- **Committed?** Uncommitted changes mean the work is not finished being recorded. Stop.
- **On a branch that is not the default?** If the commits are on the default branch, go to
  step 1a before anything else.
- **Anything to push at all?** `git log --oneline origin/<default>..HEAD` empty means there
  is nothing here. Stop and say so.
- **A change request already open for this branch?** Then this is a push, not an open. Push
  and say the existing one was updated.

Derive the default branch rather than assuming `main`.

## 1a. When the commits are on the default branch

This happens, and it is repairable. Repair it, but never silently.

**Show exactly what would move**, and move nothing else:

    git fetch origin
    git log --oneline origin/<default>..HEAD

**If anything in that list does not belong to this change, stop.** Carrying somebody else's
commits onto this branch is not a call this unit makes.

**Ask before touching history.** On a no, hand back and do not continue to the push, because
pushing from the default branch is the thing this step exists to prevent. On a yes:

    git switch -c <branch-name>
    git branch -f <default> origin/<default>

The first carries the commits onto the new branch. The second rewinds the local default to
what the remote already has. Nothing is discarded and the working tree is never touched,
which is why no hard reset appears here.

**The branch name needs the issue number.** With no issue there is nothing to name it from,
so this is the one case where a missing issue stops the run rather than degrading it.

## 2. Write the body

The issue line depends on what this change request does to its issue:

| This change request | Write | Why |
|---|---|---|
| finishes the issue | the closure keyword and the number | the issue closes on merge, not by hand |
| is one of several for it | `Part of #N` | the issue outlives this change, so a keyword would close it early |
| has no issue | nothing | and the report says this closes nothing |

**A closure keyword fires from anywhere in the body.** The parser reads the keyword and the
number and nothing around them, so a sentence explaining that this change must *not* close
#N will close it. On the middle case, write `Part of #N` and do not mention keywords at all.

Keep the body to what a reviewer needs: what changed, and what they should test. Where the
project ships a change request template, fill that instead of inventing a shape.

## 3. Open it, then read it back

**Push with tracking.** A branch cut locally has no upstream, so the first push sets one:

    git push -u origin <branch>

Without `-u` the push succeeds and later commands that ask "where does this branch go" have
no answer.

**Then create it**, body from a file rather than inline so the closure line survives quoting:

    gh   pr create --title "<title>" --body-file <file>
    glab mr create --title "<title>" --description "$(cat <file>)"

**Then read back what it actually linked**:

    gh   pr view <N> --json body,url
    glab mr view <N>

The link is the part that silently goes wrong, and the cost lands later — an issue that
closes early, or one that never closes at all.

Set whatever label marks *under review* in this project, on the issue rather than the change
request. Where the project declares no such label, say so instead of inventing one.

## 4. Stop

A human reviews and tests. This unit does not merge, does not approve, and does not wait.
Say what is open and what the reviewer should exercise, then stop.

## Steps

Copy this checklist and tick each item as you finish it:

    Task Progress:
    - [ ] Platform derived from the git remote, not assumed
    - [ ] Committed, on a non-default branch, with something to push
    - [ ] Commits moved off the default branch if they were on it, after asking
    - [ ] Body written; issue line matches what this change does to the issue
    - [ ] Pushed and opened
    - [ ] Link read back and confirmed
    - [ ] Issue label moved, or its absence stated
    - [ ] Stopped for a human

## Report

Two lines and a question:

    OPEN — PR #30 for #27, closes it on merge. Reviewer should exercise the upgrade path.
    Next: a human reviews and tests.
    Want the body?

When the commits had to be moved first, that belongs in the first line rather than the
detail, because it is the part a reviewer would not otherwise know happened:

    OPEN — PR #30 for #27, after moving three commits off main onto issue-27-parser.
    Main is back to origin; nothing was discarded.
    Next: a human reviews and tests.

An update to something already open is not a new opening:

    UPDATED — PR #30 already existed for this branch; pushed two more commits to it.
    Next: a human reviews and tests.

Refusing is a verdict too:

    NOT OPENED — the tree has uncommitted changes, so this is not finished being recorded.
    Next: commit them, then run this again.

The body, the commit list and the trace are prepared and held until asked.

input.content:
Closes #501

## What changed

The models suite failed a model for getting an answer wrong: gemma3:270m said "2" to 2+2 and the suite went red while the model loaded, sat on the GPU and unloaded cleanly. Each judge now asserts what it is good at.

- **Simple judge — did the model load and survive?** No `{"error":…}`, `done` true, a non-empty body, no CUDA error. It reads nothing of the reply's text.
- **Agent judge — is the reply language?** Readable words pass, even when wrong. Empty or junk replies fail.
- **Dual by default.** The output check now lives in the agent judge, so `test-models.yml` defaults to `judge_mode: dual`. Under `simple` alone nothing would check the output.

Supporting changes the split needed:

- **Prompt asks for a sentence** instead of a bare number. A single digit gives the agent judge nothing to call language.
- **Each step prints the reply field first**, not 2000 characters of raw body. The judge cuts each step's output at 1000 characters, and a thinking model's reasoning pushed the answer out of view.
- **TC-MODELS-016's vision and audio requests pin the sampler.** They were the only unpinned requests in the suite. Unpinned, the vision reply wandered ("arc", "heart<channel|>heart", and once 400 tokens of nothing); pinned, it's "circle" in 6 tokens.
- **The die-count check reloads once before failing.** Die placement is not deterministic — gpt-oss:20b once put 93 MiB on a third die, and it didn't reproduce. A retry prints `RELOAD:` and passes as `GPU_COUNT_OK (after one reload)`, so it's never silent. A second overshoot still fails.
- **The temperature guard is gone from the models suite.** It aborted at 80°C; the K80 itself slows at 88°C and shuts down at 93°C. Longer replies mean more GPU work, and run 35549667518 was killed at 81°C on case 9 of 19. The other six workflows keep the guard.
- **`docs/tests/TS-04-models.md`** describes the new assertions, TC-15's real six steps, and the two cases it had never listed (TC-MODELS-019, -021).

## What a reviewer should exercise

1. **A full dual run** — `test-models` with no inputs. This is the one thing not yet seen: no single full run has come back all green. Run [35551629359](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/actions/runs/35551629359) was 17/19; its two reds each pass on rerun ([35554571261](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/actions/runs/35554571261) TC-MODELS-016, [35554577681](https://github.com/dogkeeper886/ollama37/actions/runs/35554577681) TC-MODELS-001). The die-count retry has only been run locally so far.
2. **The split holds.** Already shown locally, worth a look: a fabricated empty reply passes the simple judge and fails the agent judge ("The model's reply is empty"); a model that cannot load fails the simple judge with the agent judge off.
3. **Thermals.** With the guard gone, nothing stops a run below 88°C. Worth watching `nvidia-smi` during the full run — the last green run before this change peaked at 75°C.

## Known, and not fixed here

- **The agent judge's passes say nothing.** All 17 passes read "All criteria met", with no quote of the reply. Making `evidence` required on pass would fix it, but that touches every suite.
- **`.claude/rules/workflow-patterns.md` is stale.** It still says judge mode defaults to `simple` and that the models suite runs under the temperature guard. A rewrite is planned separately.
- **#498 case 3 is stale.** It says `espeak-ng` is missing from the runner; it's installed.

## What changed

The models suite failed a model for getting an answer wrong: gemma3:270m said "2" to 2+2 and the suite went red while the model loaded, sat on the GPU and unloaded cleanly. Each judge now asserts what it is good at.

- **Simple judge — did the model load and survive?** No `{"error":…}`, `done` true, a non-empty body, no CUDA error. It reads nothing of the reply's text.

Supporting changes the split needed:

- **Prompt asks for a sentence** instead of a bare number. A single digit gives the agent judge nothing to call language.

Base directory for this skill: /home/jack/src/agent-workflows/plugins/agent-workflows/skills/land-pr

# Land the change request

Target:  — the change request to merge.

**Merge means one thing: the code is in the default branch, and the branch is merged and
deleted.** Nothing else about it interests the person who asked. Approvals, protected branch
rules, CI that must go green, a merge train, environment promotion — all of that is the
repository's route to the outcome, and this unit walks whatever route this repo requires
without asking anyone to know which.

**If the outcome cannot be reached, that is a verdict.** A failure with what blocked it, or
a revise with what must change first. The one thing this must never do is report *merged*
when the code is not in the default branch.

## 0. Which platform

Derive it from `git remote get-url origin`.

| | GitHub — `gh` | GitLab — `glab` |
|---|---|---|
| state | `gh pr view <N> --json mergeStateStatus,headRefOid,headRefName` | `glab mr view <N>` |
| comment | `gh pr comment <N> --body "…"` | `glab mr note <N> -m "…"` |
| merge | `gh pr merge <N> --merge --delete-branch` | `glab mr merge <N> --remove-source-branch` |
| **pin to a SHA** | `--match-head-commit <SHA>` | `--sha <SHA>` |

**The SHA guard is not optional here.** Both platforms can refuse a merge whose head has
moved. A gate that asks about one commit and then merges another has not gated anything, so
pass the confirmed SHA to the merge itself rather than trusting that nothing changed.

## 1. Can it merge

Read the state: conflicts, required checks, required approvals. A change request that cannot
merge does not need a human gate yet — report the blocker and stop, because asking someone
to confirm work that cannot land wastes the one thing this unit spends.

Note the head SHA now. Everything after this is pinned to it.

## 2. The human gate

**Ask outright: has this change been reviewed and tested at `<head SHA>`?**

Three things that do not answer that question, and the reason each is tempting:

- **A green agent pass.** Whatever ran before this was an agent judging its own family of
  work. This gate is a person's judgment on the change as a whole.
- **Being told to run this.** "Merge PR 30" is a request to *reach* this question, never the
  answer to it. Ask, and wait.
- **A confirmation given for a different head.** A person confirmed the diff they were
  shown. If the head has moved since — or moves mid-run — that confirmation does not carry.
  Ask again against the new SHA.

**On no, or on no answer: do not merge.** Stop and report, with the missing confirmation as
the finding. A refused gate owes the reader the same report a merge does.

**On yes, record it before merging**, so the gate leaves a trace someone can find later:

    gh   pr comment <N> --body "Human review + test confirmed at <SHA>."
    glab mr note    <N> -m     "Human review + test confirmed at <SHA>."

## 3. Merge

Pass the SHA. Use whatever strategy the project uses, and delete the source branch as part
of the merge rather than afterwards:

    gh   pr merge <N> --merge --delete-branch --match-head-commit <SHA>
    glab mr merge <N> --remove-source-branch --sha <SHA>

**Where the repo requires more than a merge command** — an approval you can request, a check
you can re-run, an auto-merge that lands it when requirements are met — do that. The outcome
is the contract, not the command.

## 4. Establish that it landed

**A command that does not return is not a failure.** It may have succeeded and lost the
connection, timed out while the platform completed it, or genuinely failed. All three look
identical from here, and retrying blind risks acting on a merge that already happened.

**Check the remote, not your working copy:**

    git fetch origin
    git log --oneline origin/<default> -5

The local copy is deliberately stale at this point. Deleting the branch returns you to the
default branch *before* the merge commit has been fetched, so every file the change touched
reads as reverted until the fetch. That intervening state is expected and is not data loss.

**Say which you established.** "Merged, verified at `<sha>` on `origin/<default>`" and
"merge state could not be established" are different reports, and only one of them is a
completion.

## 5. Clean up

**The issue.** Read the body for a closure keyword before assuming it closed:

    gh   pr view <N> --json body,closingIssuesReferences
    glab mr view <N>

With a keyword, the merge closed it. Without one, close it by hand and say that is what
happened, because an issue nobody closed reads exactly like an issue nobody finished.

**The labels.** Clear both the pipeline state and any triage state the work carried:

    gh   issue edit <issue> --remove-label <in-progress> --remove-label <triage>
    glab issue update <issue> --unlabel <in-progress> --unlabel <triage>

The triage label is the one nothing upstream removes. Skip this and it strands on closed
work forever, which is how a board fills with things that look actionable and are not.

**The branch and the tree.** The remote branch went with the merge. Remove the local one and
resolve the state step 4 warned about:

    git switch <default>
    git pull
    git branch -d <branch>

`git branch -d` refuses to delete a branch it does not consider merged. That refusal is a
signal worth reading rather than forcing: it means the merge is not visible from here yet,
usually because the pull has not run.

## Steps

Copy this checklist and tick each item as you finish it:

    Task Progress:
    - [ ] Platform derived from the git remote, not assumed
    - [ ] Mergeable — conflicts, checks and approvals read
    - [ ] Head SHA noted; everything after pinned to it
    - [ ] Human asked outright, and answered — not inferred, not assumed
    - [ ] Confirmation recorded on the change request before merging
    - [ ] Merged with the SHA passed to the merge itself
    - [ ] Landing established against the remote default branch
    - [ ] Issue closed, labels cleared, branch gone, back on the default

## Report

Two lines and a question:

    MERGED — PR #30 at a1b2c3d, verified on origin/main. #27 closed, labels cleared,
    branch gone.
    Next: nothing. This has shipped.
    Want the trace?

A refused gate is a verdict and reads the same way:

    NOT MERGED — nobody has confirmed review and test at a1b2c3d.
    Next: someone reviews and tests it, then run this again.

So is an outcome that could not be reached:

    BLOCKED — two required checks are failing, so this cannot land as it stands.
    Next: fix the checks, then run this again.

    UNKNOWN — the merge command did not return and origin/main does not show the commit.
    Next: re-check origin before retrying; a blind retry may act on a merge that landed.

The trace, the checks and the confirmation are prepared and held until asked.

content.text:
**The 63k isn't one big prompt — it's all 19 tests piling into one conversation.** A bigger context window only raises the ceiling it hits.

| Evidence | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Prompt size per test is flat** | ~7,100 characters each (TC-016 is 10,400 — it has three replies), roughly 2k tokens |
| **Judge time per test climbs anyway** | 24s at test 1, 37–45s by the middle, 57–96s by the end. Same-size prompt, growing cost — each turn reprocesses everything before it |
| **The code says why** | `agent-judge.ts:345`: *"Judge all test results, one at a time, over a single reused agent session."* Every verdict stays in the conversation for the next one |
| **The arithmetic lands on 63k** | Claude Code's own system prompt and tool definitions (~20k tokens) + 19 turns × (~2k prompt + reply) ≈ 60–65k — right at `gpt-oss-64k:20b`'s window |

**Why I'd fix the session rather than the window:**
- **128k postpones it.** The suite is 19 cases; the same accumulation fills 128k at around 40, and every test still gets slower than the one before.
- **At the limit, verdicts go bad quietly.** When the conversation outgrows `num_ctx`, ollama cuts from the front, and the front is the judge's instructions. The late tests would be judged by a model that no longer has the rules. The last run's verdicts were all correct, but it was brushing the edge.
- **The tests are independent.** Test 12 has no reason to see tests 1–11 — and a verdict that can see earlier verdicts isn't independent.
- **A fresh session per test is bounded and probably faster.** Every test would cost what test 1 cost (~24s), so about 8 minutes of judging instead of 14. The system-prompt prefix would likely be served from ollama's prompt cache.

**What I couldn't see:** SSH to [REDACTED-private-ip] is refused for me, so I haven't read that container's log. If you paste `docker logs --tail 200 <container>` from there, the thing to look for is ollama's truncation line (`truncating input prompt` or a context shift) near the end of a judge run. That would confirm the window actually overflowed rather than just getting close.

Your plan (compose down, bring up system ollama, build a 96k/128k Modelfile) is still available as a stopgap. Want me to make the per-test session change instead, or as well?

content.text:
The log confirms the accumulation to the token, and corrects one thing I told you.

**Per judge request on `onyx`, during the last full run:**

| Request | Prompt tokens | Cached | Prompt eval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Side call | 433 | 0 | 0.4s |
| Availability probe | 20,562 | 0 | 10.3s |
| Test 1 | 23,127 | 0 | 12.1s |
| Test 5 | 33,248 | 0 | 19.9s |
| Test 10 | 46,726 | 0 | 34.5s |
| Test 15 | 59,358 | 0 | 49.7s |
| Test 17 (peak) | **64,342** | 0 | 57.4s |
| Tests 18–19 | ~63,500 | 0 | ~56s |

What it shows:

- **Claude Code's baseline is ~20.5k tokens** before any test data — its system prompt and tool definitions.
- **Each test adds ~2,500 tokens and never leaves.** 23k at test 1 climbs steadily to 64,342 — **98% of the 65,536-token slot**. That's your 63k.
- **Nothing overflowed.** Every request reports `truncated = 0`. The dip to ~63.5k on the last two looks like Claude Code trimming its own history near the limit. A 20th case would likely have tipped it.
- **The cache hit is zero on every request.** Each call reprocessed the whole conversation from scratch. The log is full of `erased invalidated context checkpoint … n_swa` lines: gpt-oss uses sliding-window attention, and llama-server can't reuse its prefix cache here. So **I was wrong earlier** that a fresh session's system prompt would come from cache. It won't, on this model.
- **Most of the judging time is re-reading history.** Prompt eval alone sums to roughly 11 of the 14 judging minutes, and it grows linearly because every test reprocesses all the tests before it.

**What that means for the two options:**

| | Per-test session | 128k Modelfile |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens per test | ~23k, flat | Grows ~2.5k per test, without limit |
| Prompt eval per test | ~12s, flat (no cache, so it pays the 20.5k baseline every time) | 12s → 57s at 19 tests, and keeps climbing |
| Judging, 19 tests | ~4 min of prefill | Same ~11 min as now |
| Cases before overflow | Never, at this suite's shape | ~40 |
| Each verdict sees earlier ones | No | Yes |

The per-test session is the fix. The bigger window buys headroom for a longer suite but keeps the slowdown. They aren't exclusive — if you do bring up the 96k/128k model for other reasons, per-test sessions still apply on top of it.

Step 1 done. What's step 2?

content.text:
Current flow first, then the proposed one. Function names are from `cicd/tests/src/judge/agent-judge.ts`; token counts are from the `onyx` log.

**Current — one session for the whole run**

```
  isAvailable()
      │
      ▼
  ensureStarted() ── spawn ACP agent ── initialize ── session/new ──► session S
      │
      ▼
  probe turn on S  ("Reply with exactly: ok")              S = 20.5k tokens
      │
      ▼
  ┌───────────── for each of 19 tests ─────────────┐
  │  judgeOne(test)                                 │
  │      │                                          │
  │      ▼                                          │
  │  prompt on S  ◄── S still holds every earlier   │
  │      │            test + verdict                 │     test 1  → 23.1k
  │      ▼                                          │     test 10 → 46.7k
  │  llama-server re-reads ALL of S (cache = 0)     │     test 17 → 64.3k  ◄ 98% of 65,536
  │      │                                          │
  │      ▼                                          │     prefill 12s → 57s
  │  verdict appended to S ─────────────────────────┘     (grows every test)
      │
      ▼
  kill agent
```

**Proposed — a fresh session per test, one agent process**

```
  isAvailable()
      │
      ▼
  ensureStarted() ── spawn ACP agent ── initialize          (process kept for the whole run)
      │
      ▼
  session/new ──► P ── probe turn ── discard P               P = 20.5k tokens
      │
      ▼
  ┌───────────── for each of 19 tests ─────────────┐
  │  session/new ──► T  (empty: rules + this test)  │
  │      │                                          │
  │      ▼                                          │
  │  prompt on T                                    │     every test → ~23k
  │      │                                          │
  │      ▼                                          │     prefill ~12s, flat
  │  llama-server reads T only                      │
  │      │                                          │
  │      ▼                                          │
  │  verdict ── discard T ──────────────────────────┘
      │
      ▼
  kill agent

  on timeout (unchanged): kill agent ──► next test re-spawns ──► session/new
```

**What changes**

| | Current | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| Sessions per run | 1 | 1 probe + 1 per test |
| Agent processes | 1 (re-spawned only after a timeout) | 1, same |
| Tokens per test | 23k → 64k, growing | ~23k, flat |
| Prefill per test | 12s → 57s | ~12s |
| A verdict can see earlier tests | Yes | No |
| Overflow at | ~20 tests | Never, at this suite's shape |

**The code change is small.** `ensureStarted()` would stop at the agent handshake. `session/new` moves to the top of each `judgeOne()`, and the session is dropped after the verdict. Spawning, the timeout-and-respawn path, and the probe's fallback to the simple judge all stay as they are. Because it lives in the shared judge, every suite run in dual mode gets the fix, not just models.

Want this as a page you can share, or shall I go ahead and make the change?

content.text:
You're right that prefill is the cost to watch, but `/clear` wouldn't save it — and my proposal doesn't start a new agent. Here's what the code and log say:

| Your concern | What the evidence says |
|---|---|
| **A new agent per test means a model load** | My proposal keeps **one agent process** for the whole run and only opens a new *session* on it. And even a new process wouldn't reload the model: the model lives on `onyx`, and the log shows one `starting llama-server` at 02:12:50 for the entire run. The agent only sends HTTP requests to it |
| **A new session means a 24k prefill per test** | True — but **every request pays that today too**. The log shows `cached = 0` on all 21 requests, including those with a byte-identical prefix. gpt-oss's sliding-window attention invalidates llama-server's cache every time. So a fresh session costs ~23k per test, which is what today's flow pays at test 1 and less than every test after it |
| **Use `/clear` instead** | It doesn't work over ACP. `claude-agent-acp` lists `"clear"` in its `UNSUPPORTED_COMMANDS` (`acp-agent.js:2848`). Opening a new ACP session on the same connection is ACP's equivalent of `/clear` — same effect, no new process |
| **Judge only after all tests finish** | Agreed, and it already works that way. `cli.ts:140–156` runs every test, then the simple judge, then the agent judge over all results. The judge model loads once and stays hot through back-to-back verdicts. Nothing in the proposal changes that |

So `/clear` and a new session land in the same place: history gone, ~23k tokens per test, one process, one model load.

**The bigger lever on your prefill concern is the 20.5k baseline itself.** That's mostly Claude Code's tool definitions, and the judge never uses tools — it already rejects every tool request. If the judge's session is opened with its tools disabled, that baseline could shrink a lot, and it would help both flows. The verifier judge already passes options this way (`_meta.claudeCode.options` in `verifier-judge.ts`). I haven't measured how far it drops, so treat that as a hypothesis until one probe run shows the token count.

Updated proposal:
1. One agent process per run, as today.
2. A new session per test (ACP's `/clear`).
3. Tools off in the judge session, if the probe shows it shrinks the baseline.
4. Judging stays after all tests complete.

Want me to measure step 3 first? One probe against `onyx`, reading the token count from its log.

content.text:
Tools off shrinks the judge's baseline by 92%, and a second session on the same process costs the same as the first — no reload.

**Measured on `onyx`, one agent process, three sessions, one "Reply with exactly: ok" turn each:**

| Session | Prompt tokens | Prefill | Round trip | Reply |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A — tools default (today's judge) | **19,875** | 9.5s | 21.2s ¹ | `okok` |
| B — `tools: []` | **1,505** | 0.9s | 10.9s | `okok` |
| C — `tools: []`, 2nd session, same process | **1,505** | 0.9s | 5.8s | `okok` |

¹ A also absorbed a cold start: the model had expired on `onyx` and `starting llama-server` fired at 03:05:10. Compare tokens, not A's wall time.

What this settles:

- **The 20k baseline is almost all tool definitions.** Without them Claude Code's prompt is ~1.5k tokens.
- **No reload per session.** B and C ran on one agent process with one llama-server start. C, a plain second session, took 5.8s end to end.
- **Each session adds a small side call.** Every session triggered a ~434-token request (Claude Code's background housekeeping). About 0.3s each — negligible.
- **The cache still never hits** (`cached n_tokens = 0` on every new prompt), so shrinking the prompt is what actually saves time. `/clear` wouldn't have.
- **The doubled reply is a model habit, not our code.** It shows up as `okok` even in this bare probe.

**Projected for a 19-case run:** each test ≈ 1.5k baseline + ~2.5k test data ≈ **4k tokens**, flat — versus 23k climbing to 64k today. Judging should drop from ~14 min to roughly 2–3 min, and the 64k window stops mattering: at 4k per test even the stock context is plenty.

One thing is unproven: that verdicts stay as good with tools off. The judge never used tools, so I expect no change, but it should be checked on real judge prompts — the empty-reply probe plus a full run.

The change to `agent-judge.ts` is small:
1. Keep one process, as today.
2. Open a new session per test, passing `tools: []`.
3. Leave judging after all tests complete, and leave the timeout/respawn path untouched.

Shall I make it on a branch and run the probes and a full suite against it?

content.text:
**No — the judge doesn't need the tools.** The replay also turned up a cost of fresh sessions I hadn't measured: one extra model call per session.

**Verdicts — 19 real judge inputs, each judged in a fresh session:**

| | Original run | Tools on | Tools off |
|---|---|---|---|
| Verdicts matching the original | — | 19 / 19 | 19 / 19 |
| The two real FAILs caught | TC-001, TC-016 | Both | Both |
| Times the judge asked to use a tool | — | **0** of 19 | 0 of 19 |

Reasons on the FAILs match too. For TC-016, tools off said *"Vision inference returned empty content"*. With tools on, the judge never even asked to use one — they were 18k tokens of dead weight in every request.

**Cost per request, from `onyx`'s log:**

| Request | Prompt | Prefill | Generated | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Judgement, tools on | 22,389 tok | 11.5s | 750 tok, 12.2s | **23.8s** |
| Judgement, tools off | 3,995 tok | 1.8s | 878 tok, 13.1s | **15.0s** |
| **Side call, once per new session** | 2,903 tok | 1.4s | 848 tok, 12.6s | **14.0s** |

**What that changes in the proposal:**

- **Tools off is a clear win.** The prompt shrinks 82%, and prefill drops from 11.5s to 1.8s. What's left is generation: gpt-oss reasons for ~850 tokens before answering, whatever the prompt size.
- **Your instinct about fresh sessions was right, for a reason neither of us named.** It isn't prefill or a model load — it's the side call. Every new session makes one extra request that carries the test prompt (~2.9k tokens) and generates ~850 tokens of reasoning, ~14s. That's about as expensive as the judgement itself.
  - It looks like Claude Code's background session-titling call. I route that "haiku" slot to gpt-oss through `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`, so it reasons like everything else.
  - Today's single-session run paid it once, on the short probe (433 tokens).
- **Net, per test:**

| Flow | Per test | 19 tests | Bounded? |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Today: one session, tools on | 24s → 96s, climbing | ~14 min | No — 98% of the window at test 17 |
| Fresh session + tools off (measured) | ~29s | ~9 min | Yes |
| Fresh session + tools off + no side call (projected) | ~15s | ~5 min | Yes |

**Next lever: kill the side call.** Claude Code has a `DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS=1` setting that should suppress background calls like titling. It's untested here. Replaying three or four cases with it set would show whether the 2.9k-token requests disappear from `onyx`'s log.

The replay script lives in the scratchpad (`replay-judge.ts`). It rebuilds any finished run's judge inputs byte-exact and replays them under a changed configuration. That's a reusable way to test judge changes without re-running the models — worth keeping in `cicd/tests` if you want it.

Want me to try the side-call switch next?
